target_customer: Music fans and indie artists on a free, ad-driven social music site
problem: Discovering new singles is dominated by labels and radio; fans have no community vote to surface unknown songs.
business_model: Consumer web site, advertising supported (not stated by sources)
product_category: Social music discovery with Digg-style voting

founders.name: Shadab Farooqui
founders.background_notes: Spelled Frooqui in Vator headlines. CEO per the Vator interview titles. A Vator headline gives his age as 26 in April 2008; not used as founding age.

founders.name: Zaid Farooqui
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page

founders.name: Bilal Farooqui
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; YC page team size says 2

competitors.name: ContraStream
competitors.what: Social music site with user-voted tracks, called the closer competitor

competitors.name: Last.fm
competitors.what: Social music discovery and scrobbling service

competitors.name: Pandora
competitors.what: Streaming stations built from the Music Genome Project

competitors.name: iLike
competitors.what: Social music service named on the YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Flash music player, voting and embedding on MySpace; standard consumer web engineering in 2007 for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Community votes could create a small network effect but rivals such as ContraStream copied the Digg voting idea and the site offered no way to buy or download songs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large music services crowded the space; the company is listed Inactive and the domain ijigg.com is now for sale.

market_need_then: VentureBeat reported over 130,000 registered users, about 1,700 new per day and 12 million page views in a month by August 2007, so there was user interest in indie music voting.

branding.name_origin: The name plays on Digg; TechCrunch (2007-01-18) headlined the launch as 'Jigg That Music' and the pitch was Digg for music. No founder statement of the origin found.
branding.domain_note: ijigg.com was the exact domain; it is now offered for sale for 4,888 USD (checked 2026).
branding.community_and_virality: Embedding songs on MySpace drove spread; TechCrunch and VentureBeat covered it in 2007.

brand_strength.rationale: Derivative of Digg and easily misspelled, though it earned press coverage and a catchy verb. The Top440 name appears on the YC listing without a dated source for the rename.

outcome_analysis: iJigg grew to over 130,000 registered users within months of launch in 2007 and was raising an angel round in August 2007, but it competed with Last.fm, Pandora, iLike and MySpace and focused on little-known international music. YC lists it Inactive and no source states a cause or date of shutdown, so the failure factors are inferred from the crowded market.
notes: VentureBeat says YC backed it in April 2007 and an angel round was in progress in Aug 2007; no amount or angel closing found. The Vator article returned 404 when fetched, so its claims come from the search snippet only (seed from YC, CEO and age 26 in 2008). Cause of inactivity not public in sources found. Company site ijigg.com is a domain for sale page. Competitor entries dated Aug 2007 are within a few months of the batch.
